commit 545039733b74eec742862f161990142c7ca7c7ec (the head of main when these files were taken, 2026-10-21)
vendored v4895 (unnumbered until shipped): FIVE FILES, byte for byte, each fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at that commit and compared with the copy the v4895 survey had read:
  LICENSE                                   (the permission notice; it travels with every portion, as the licence requires)
  src/shaders/deformSim.fragment.wgsl       242 lines   the toroidal deformation pass: scroll, relax (diffusion, wind infill, slump, decay), splat, clamp
  src/shaders/lib/noise.wgsl                            snowNoise: the hashes and the gradient noise the pass's brush edge uses
  src/shaders/lib/deform.wgsl               74 lines    how the terrain material reads the buffer (not adapted yet)
  src/terrain/deformation.js                295 lines   the driver: ping-pong targets, brush queue, the banked-time rule
tools/ship/snowflowVendor-selfcheck.mjs pins every file's sha256 and states what each is.
WHAT IT IS: the surface-deformation half of a WebGPU snow demo built on Babylon.js. Its shaders are Babylon-flavoured WGSL (#include<...>, loose `uniform name: type;` declarations,
FragmentInputs/FragmentOutputs), so they do NOT run as they are; render/toroidalDeform.mjs is SweK's own adaptation, a compute kernel over plain storage buffers whose function bodies are
these files' bodies, with a CPU twin that grades it. NOTHING NOT LISTED ABOVE WAS TAKEN: the rest of the repository (the character, cloth, spells, water and sky passes, the Babylon wiring,
README and package files) is not here, and nothing here depends on Babylon.js or Vite.
NOT VERIFIED BY RUNNING UPSTREAM: the sandbox did not run the demo; its README's frame-time figure is its own claim. What IS run is our adaptation, against our own CPU twin.
